content.text: Okay, I'll ask them to contact you.

Sure thing! Please have your colleague get in touch with us and provide the email address they used for the purchase along with the order number. Once we have that information, we’ll be able to verify the order and process the refund if it meets our policy. Let us know if there’s anything else we can help with in the meantime.

Customer says they'll ask colleague to contact. We could offer to help but need verification. Could handoff? The request is ambiguous. We can ask if they have the order ID or email. But they said they'll ask them to contact. Probably we should handoff to human to avoid back-and-forth. According to policy, handoff when customer asks for a human. They didn't explicitly ask, but they said they'll ask them to contact you. Could still proceed. Better to ask for clarification: "Do you have the order ID?" But we already asked. They responded with "Okay, I'll ask them to contact you." That suggests they will have the colleague contact. We can respond politely: "Sure, please have them reach out with their email and order number, and we’ll be happy to help." No need to handoff.
